summary: This survey covers participating postsecondary institutions’ undergraduate and graduate enrollment and instructional activity during the 12-month period from July 1, 2016, through June 30, 2017. It is institution-level and covers activity across the full year rather than a single term, including institutions with nontraditional calendars or short-term programs where applicable.

The Completions survey covers awards and degree or certificate recipients at eligible postsecondary institutions for the reporting period July 1, 2016, through June 30, 2017. Its unit of observation is the institution or an institution-level breakdown record, and the universe is institutions that report postsecondary completions and related program offerings. Counts describe awards or students receiving awards during that period, while program-offering counts are derived from those completions.

These tables cover fall enrollment reported by postsecondary institutions, with UNITID as the institution-level identifier; tables can contain multiple records per institution keyed by their respective student or enrollment dimensions. Traditional academic-year institutions report enrollment as of October 15 or their official fall reporting date, while institutions with differing or continuous calendars report students enrolled at any time from August 1 through October 31. Eligibility and reporting caveats that apply only to particular measures, such as undergraduate-only coverage or optional-year reporting, are noted in the individual table summaries.

The Finance component was collected December 13, 2017–April 11, 2018 and reports institutions’ finances for fiscal year 2017; reporting is annual and required for postsecondary institutions participating in Title IV federal aid programs. The unit of observation is the institution (one finance record per institution), with institutions assigned to the accounting-model and ownership forms below. Beginning with fiscal year 2016, detailed expenditures by function and the natural classifications of fringe benefits, operations and maintenance of plant, depreciation, and interest are not available.

Graduation Rates reports institution-level outcomes for full-time, first-time degree/certificate-seeking undergraduates, with student status measured as of August 31, 2017. Institutions are represented through cohorts defined by sector or program length and tracked for completion and, where applicable, transfer within specified percentages of normal time. The relevant universe is institutions enrolling these eligible undergraduate cohorts; cohort years and the applicable completion windows vary by table.

The Human Resources survey describes institutional employees and new hires, with payroll staff generally counted as of November 1; salary tables report staff and salary outlays for the academic year. The unit of observation is an institution-by-staff-category record, so institutions can have multiple records, with eligibility and coverage varying by table, including degree-granting institutions with at least 15 full-time employees for several instructional-staff and new-hire tables. Race/ethnicity and gender reporting was mandatory annually beginning in 2016; earlier rules made it mandatory in odd-numbered years and optional in even-numbered years.

Institutional Characteristics is collected annually in the fall for institutions in the 2017-18 IPEDS universe. Title IV-participating institutions are required to report; other institutions in the IPEDS universe may be included where applicable. The data are institution-level, although some tables attach records to survey components or comparison-group memberships.

The Student Financial Aid survey covers aid received during July 1, 2016–June 30, 2017 and reports institution-level counts and dollar amounts. It covers institutions in the IPEDS reporting universe, with eligibility and student populations varying by table; records are summarized by institution and applicable student group rather than by individual student.
